headword: {後塵|こうじん}を{拝|はい}する
gloss: to fall behind; to be outdone by

definitions.gloss: to fall behind someone; to be outperformed; to be left in the dust
definitions.explanation: An idiomatic expression meaning to be surpassed or outpaced by someone. Literally means "to bow to someone's trailing dust" — the image of following behind someone's carriage and being covered in their dust.

examples.japanese: ⟦ライバル→ライバル：11197_raibaru⟧⟦{企業|きぎょう}→企業：00225_kigyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{後塵|こうじん}を{拝|はい}する。
examples.english: To fall behind the rival company.

examples.japanese: ⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦{開発|かいはつ}→開発：06746_kaihatsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{他国|たこく}→他国：28893_takoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{後塵|こうじん}を{拝|はい}して⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: We are lagging behind other countries in technological development.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{分野|ぶんや}→分野：03612_bunya⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧{後塵|こうじん}を{拝|はい}してきた⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、ようやく{追|お}いついてきた。
examples.english: We had been trailing behind for years in this field, but we have finally caught up.

notes:
Literally "to bow to (someone's) trailing dust." The image comes from ancient China, where a person of lower rank would follow behind a dignitary's carriage and be covered in the dust it raised. By extension, it means to be inferior to or behind someone.

COMMON PATTERNS:
～⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{後塵|こうじん}を{拝|はい}する — to fall behind ~

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦ライバル→ライバル：11197_raibaru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{後塵|こうじん}を{拝|はい}する: to fall behind a rival
- ⟦{他社|たしゃ}→他社：17803_tasha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{後塵|こうじん}を{拝|はい}する: to lag behind other companies
- {後塵|こうじん}を{拝|はい}し⟦{続|つづ}ける→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧: to continue trailing behind

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{遅|おく}れ→遅れ：01908_okure⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to fall behind — more common and less literary
- ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}けられる→開ける：00563_akeru⟧: to have a gap opened up — used when the distance between competitors widens
- ⟦{引|ひ}け→引く：01978_hiku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}らない→取る：00565_toru⟧: to be no less than — the positive counterpart: not falling behind
